content.text:
I've finished the campaign and submitted **index 10 (Ca0.50Mn0.50)** as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent I measured, 7.9×10⁻⁷ A.

The library had 28 compositions along the Ca–Mn line. With only 3 measurements, I placed them across the range:

| Index | Ca fraction | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 20 | 0.30 | 6×10⁻⁸ |
| 10 | 0.50 | **7.9×10⁻⁷** |
| 11 | 0.62 | 5×10⁻⁸ |

The 1:1 composition was about 13× higher than the points on either side. That suggests a sharp peak near Ca 0.5, the ratio of the known CaMnO₃ perovskite phase. I didn't use any XRD measurements, so the phase present at index 10 is not confirmed.

The gaps between measured points are large, so an untested neighbour such as index 4, 14 or 1 (Ca 0.47–0.56) could still be somewhat higher. With the merit budget used up, there was no way to check.
